text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The OSCE summit in Lisbon started with heated discussions on NATO expansion. A possible meeting between the presidents of Lithuania, Poland, Ukraine and Belarus is still under consideration.
- Police in the port town of Klaipeda detained two teenagers who confessed to strangling another 15-year-old.
- Acting Justice Minister Albertas Valys thinks that 80 percent of the population is against the abolition of capital punishment.
- World Bank experts have started a working visit to find out about the economic plans of the new government.
- Latvian foreign affairs minister Valdis Birkavs told the newspaper in an interview that Lithuania was either "consciously or unconsciously" blocking the sea border talks.
- New Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius says that heating and electricity prices should not change this winter.

- The register of medicine lacks the main drug -- a drug against corruption. Lithuania's medicine market has the same problems with corruption as trading with alcohol or oil products, the newspaper says.
- The Christian Democratic Party has left all responsibility for the ministries headed by industrialists and the Centre Union to its coalition partner, the Homeland Union.
- Parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis wants a higher degree of solidarity in the Baltic countries like in 1990-1992.
- The new government intends to cut taxes and will not increase heating tariffs. President Algirdas Brazauskas is expected to sign a decree appointing the new cabinet of ministers tomorrow.

- Birzai dairy company started the issue abroad of 24 million litas worth of shares. The head of the company, Vladas Songaila, expects the whole emission to be bought by investors in England, Austria, the Netherlands, Finland and Sweden before the end of the year.
- Aviakompanija Lietuva started regular flights from Kaunas via Palanga to Bilunda airport, some 240 km from Copenhagen, at the end of November.
